h: Paying on the Nail in the Old City
p: Corn Street has a famous bit of history right on the pavement. Outside the old Exchange building stand the brass "nails", flat-topped pillars where merchants once did their deals. Legend has it they gave us the phrase "paying on the nail", so it's worth a look before or after your session. St Nicholas Market, just next door, is a great spot for a bite to eat, with a buzzing mix of street food and quirky stalls.

If you're planning a group night out, a few pointers. Book for the right number of players and arrive a little early so you can grab a drink and get settled. If you've got a big crowd, consider splitting into teams across a couple of oches so everyone gets plenty of throws.

New to darts? Here's a tip. Stand side-on with your front foot towards the oche, keep your elbow still and throw with a smooth flick of the forearm. Follow through towards the board. You'll be surprised how quickly your aim improves when you stop trying to throw too hard.

Bristol is a city that rewards wandering. After your session, head for the Harbourside or the colourful streets of Clifton, or grab a drink by the water. Christmas time is especially lively, with festive parties filling the city, so book well ahead if you're planning a December do. Bristol's work-party season fills up early, and the best slots for bigger groups are usually the first to go.
